subject.title: fix(memory): recover real on-disk path for slugified QMD search results

question: Should recovered filesystem aliases become an accepted indexed-read identity, and if so should that identity be prepared during QMD refresh rather than discovered during each search/read request?
rationale: The patch intentionally changes which on-disk paths satisfy the indexed-memory read boundary, and choosing the durable source of truth requires Memory/QMD owner intent rather than an automated mechanical repair.

options.title: Prepare Canonical Alias Map
options.body: Build and validate a process-stable, ambiguity-rejecting mapping during collection refresh, then use it for both result resolution and indexed reads.

options.title: Accept Request-Time Recovery
options.body: Keep the proposed disk recovery only after owner approval and native-QMD latency, containment, and roundtrip proof across realistic collections.

options.title: Require Upstream QMD Fix
options.body: Avoid broadening OpenClaw read identity and resolve the active-row path defect in native QMD before landing a narrower defensive check.

recommendation.title: Prepare Canonical Alias Map
recommendation.body: Build and validate a process-stable, ambiguity-rejecting mapping during collection refresh, then use it for both result resolution and indexed reads.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository identifies this person with Memory/QMD ownership and the backend's original implementation history.
